reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is vague and lacks scientific grounding; it does not specify which HEA, how it is added, or why an HEA would reduce thermal boundary resistance, and it ignores the well-known trade-off that adding a phase usually decreases thermal conductivity in metal-matrix composites.
reasons.testability: A comparative experiment is outlined, but the hypothesis is so poorly defined (no HEA composition, no processing route, no irradiation conditions) that the test cannot be executed as written, and the falsification criteria are circular.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is too generic to guide research; it merely restates the goal without providing a concrete, actionable intervention or mechanism, offering no insight to a researcher working on this problem.
